transcript:
Meeting Header: 2025-07-19 16:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Alex Carter, Samir Patel - Redwood; Jenna Liu, Ramon Ortega, Priya Menon, Elliot Shaw - CedarLane

Summary (auto): quick governance check to map who signs off on MSA/DPA, escalation lanes for priv keys/KMS, pricing guardrails for pilot and who owns security review. AE+SE-led; customer wanted clarity on dedicated vs hosted and on egress/KMS options.

00:00 Alex Carter: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we have about an hour, i'll kick off — high level today is governance and what the procurement path looks like for a pilot, MSA redline expectations, and what security needs to see for KMS and SSO.
00:18 Jenna Liu: thanks Alex uh we are on a tight calendar — finance needs a ballpark, procurement team wants a single page of risks ok
00:32 Ramon Ortega: hi quick note from security perspective we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs retention, and we have a preference for customer-managed keys, ideally HSM-backed, is that supported?
00:46 Samir Patel: yes we support KMS integrations, and for private deployments we can do customer-managed HSM, for hosted we offer a SaaS KMS option and optional BYOK; the audit logs retention is configurable — i'll add the specifics but it typically includes request/response metadata and token level usage metrics.
01:08 Priya Menon: and from m-l ops standpoint the important thing is latency and cost switch, our product is latency sensitive for the nimble-infer endpoints — we want to understand dedicated GPU pool pricing vs hosted credits.
01:26 Alex Carter: good flag, we typically present three lanes — hosted low friction (pay-as-you-go), dedicated reserved for predictable throughput, and private for compliance; each has different SLA and cost math. Samir can go through a matrix.
01:40 Samir Patel: yeah so the matrix — sorry my screen is flipping — hosted SLO around 200ms tail latency for TTR workloads, dedicated can do consistent 80-120ms depending on model and config, cost per token is lower on dedicated if you're committed, we can run a pilot to measure real qps and give a firm estimate.
02:12 Elliot Shaw: on the MSA — are there standard indemnity limits? we may need to request a lower cap for data processing — also DPA clause for data residency, we operate under EU regs for some customers.
02:30 Alex Carter: our standard MSA has a commercial cap but we can discuss redlines; i'll send the standard + call out the DPA section. we have a redline template that highlights privacy and keying.
02:44 Jenna Liu: procurement asks about third-party subprocessors, do you publish a list and how often is it updated?
02:52 Samir Patel: yes we maintain a subprocessors registry, updated quarterly; for private deployments you get an ops runbook with full host list.
03:10 Ramon Ortega: about egress costs — we need clarity on network egress for high-volume embeddings, is that billed separately?
03:18 Alex Carter: egress is handled usally as part of the infra line item, for hosted there may be egress fees depending on region — we'll include a placeholder in the pricing spreadsheet. also there was a previous note mentioned about model quantization and unit token changes, that impacts pricing too.
03:45 Priya Menon: regarding the pilot success metrics — we want 95th p99 latency under X ms for 10k qps, accuracy drift <= 1% relative to baseline, and cost per 1k tokens under the threshold — can you confirm you can instrument those?
04:02 Samir Patel: yes instrumentation is standard, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency, and tracing hooks; we can put in a shared eval prompt set for drift alerts.
04:22 Elliot Shaw: security checklist: SSO (SAML/SCIM), mfa, role-based access control, audit log retention, and encryption at-rest including keys lifecycle management. do you have SOC2 type 2 and penetration testing reports?
04:40 Samir Patel: we have SOC2 type II reports on request, and annual pentests, i'll share the security package link after call. for SSO we support SAML and SCIM; RBAC granularity is at org/route level.
05:00 Jenna Liu: timeline — we need procurement approval by July 31 to hit our pilot by mid-august — is that doable?
05:08 Alex Carter: yes if we get a signed procurement intake and we unblock legal, pilot can start mid-aug. I'll produce a one-page risks summary for your governance committee.
05:18 Priya Menon: can you also outline rollback/rollback SLA and fallback model variants if capacity constrained? we want graceful degradation.
05:27 Samir Patel: absolutely — runtime supports smart routing and fallbacks. we can define canary and fallback policies in rollout config — i'll include defaults in the SLA matrix.
05:40 Elliot Shaw: one question on escrow and logs retention for e-discovery — do you support 7-year retention if needed?
05:50 Alex Carter: long retentions are supported for private deployments; for hosted we can extend retention for a fee — i'll include options.
06:02 Ramon Ortega: any regulators we should call out? we have a EU customer base, data residency is important.
06:10 Alex Carter: noted — we'll call out EU region hosting and on-prem options, plus DPA redlines for residency.
06:22 Jenna Liu: ok next steps, can you put the MSA redlines and a pricing pilot estimate in one email? procurement needs a clean deck.
06:30 Alex Carter: yes we'll send a packet: MSA/DPA redlines, pricing spreadsheet (hosted/dedicated/private lanes), security package link, and a short pilot runbook.
06:38 Priya Menon: also include a sample traffic pattern CSV so we can validate the cost model.
06:45 Samir Patel: noted — i'll include throughput assumptions and recommended batching/kv cache suggestions to hit latency targets.
06:55 Elliot Shaw: we'll review legal redlines and loop in our counsel; expect feedback by 2025-07-23.
07:05 Alex Carter: perfect — recap: action items on file, we'll aim to send materials by 2025-07-22, procurement to confirm budget gate by 2025-07-21 and legal to send redline by 2025-07-23. thanks everyone.
